record.notes: Issued 3 Apr 2025. It applies to contracts awarded under solicitations issued on or after 30 Sep 2025, 180 days after issuance, and to options to renew or extend the period of performance exercised on existing contracts after that date; date_in_force is that date. Agencies had 270 days to update their internal acquisition procedures. It does not apply to AI acquired as a component of a National Security System or to elements of the Intelligence Community. It rescinds and replaces OMB M-24-18, Advancing the Responsible Acquisition of Artificial Intelligence in Government.

verification.note: Recheck of 17 Oct 2026: re-read the whitehouse.gov PDF of M-25-22 stored on 11 Oct 2026 (the archiver found it unchanged on 17 Oct 2026; Last-Modified 4 Apr 2025). It confirms the memo number, title, 3 Apr 2025 date, the Office of Management and Budget as issuer, the rescission and replacement of M-24-18, the contract requirements in the summary, the exclusions and the 180-day application rule. The application date of 30 Sep 2025 is calculated from that rule. The stored text shows no later amendment or replacement; OMB M-26-04 of Dec 2025 (US-19) describes itself as complementing M-25-22.

status.quote: This memorandum shall apply to any contract awarded pursuant to a solicitation issued on or after the date that is 180 days after issuance of this memorandum

legal_force.quote: agencies must include terms that address the following in contracts for AI systems and services

notes.quote: as well as to any option to renew or extend the period of performance exercised on an existing contract after the date that is 180 days after the issuance of this memorandum
Within 270 days of the issuance of this memorandum, agencies must revisit, and update where necessary, existing internal procedures on acquisition
This memorandum does not apply to AI acquired for use as a component of a National Security System.
The requirements in this memorandum do not apply to elements of the Intelligence Community
This memorandum rescinds and replaces 0MB Memorandum M-24-18, Advancing the Responsible Acquisition ofArtificial Intelligence in Government.

summary.quote: make an initial determination of whether a system is likely to host high-impact AI use cases
Contracts must ensure compliance with minimum risk management practices for high-impact use cases as required under M-25-21.

Ensuring contracts permanently prohibit the use of non public inputted agency data and outputted results to further train publicly or commercially available AI algorithms, consistent with applicable law, absent explicit agency consent

changes.notes: 'about 30 Sep 2025' made exact (3 Apr 2025 plus 180 days is 30 Sep 2025); the options-to-renew clause, the 270-day procedure update and M-24-18's full title added from the memo; the date 'Oct 2024' for M-24-18 removed because the stored text does not give it

judgment.status_reasoning: Issued 3 April 2025; it applies to solicitations issued on or after the date 180 days after issuance. 3 April 2025 plus 180 days is 30 September 2025 (27 days to 30 April, then 31+30+31+31 to 31 August = 150, plus 30 days of September = 180). That date has passed, and the stored file shows no amendment or rescission. 'In force' stands as of 17 Oct 2026.
judgment.scope_reasoning: AI-specific, binding government-wide guidance on federal acquisition of AI with risk management requirements; in scope with no note.
judgment.date_reasoning: date_published is the memo's date, 3 April 2025. date_in_force stays 30 September 2025, the date from which the memo applies to new solicitations and option exercises, computed from Section 2(c); the agency-level tasks run from issuance and are described in notes.
judgment.summary_reasoning: The current summary is supported: Section 4(a)(ii) (initial high-impact determination), Section 4(d) contract terms that agencies must include (M-25-21 compliance, ongoing testing and monitoring, vendor performance, new feature notification), Section 3(e)(iv) (no training on non-public agency data without consent) and Section 3(c) (maximise use of American-made AI). Left unchanged.
